findings.title: Example zone has no CAA record restricting certificate issuance for holden-test.example.com.
findings.explanation: The module's `records` variable already accepts type "CAA" (see variables.tf validation), but the example zone defined only A/MX/TXT records and no CAA record. Without a CAA record, any publicly-trusted CA can issue a certificate for holden-test.example.com. after passing domain validation, with no way for the domain owner to restrict issuance to a chosen set of CAs. Holden had no rule for this because google_dns_record_set has zero deterministic coverage — it can't express "a record of type X must exist for this zone", which is exactly what requires_companion is for (see suggested_policies).
findings.remediation: Add a CAA record entry to the `records` list in example/examplea/module.dns.tf restricting issuance to the CA(s) actually used for this domain.

suggested_policies.rationale: google_dns_record_set has zero entries in coverage_by_type — no deterministic rule inspects record content at all. A permissive/unqualified SPF "all" mechanism is one of the most common real-world DNS misconfigurations enabling domain-spoofed phishing email, is fully attribute-based (rrdatas is a []string on a single resource), and none_match already exists as an operator for exactly this shape (list-element regex fail-condition), so no DSL extension is needed. Imported locally as HLD_GCP_469 and submitted upstream on branch feat/hld-gcp-469-spf-no-permissive-all (push succeeded to the JamesWoolfenden/holden fork; PR to PaloAltoNetworks/holden blocked by org SAML SSO from this session). Note: this was originally assigned HLD_GCP_467 via `holden next-id`, but that ID collided with an unrelated Cloud Workflows policy merged locally to the fork's main branch by a concurrent session in the same shared clone — renumbered to 469 (next-id re-run against the fork's full local state, including the concurrent session's commits) before pushing, and the origin branch/commit were renamed/amended accordingly.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_469
name: SPF TXT records must not use a permissive or unqualified "all" mechanism
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  An SPF record's "all" mechanism controls what happens for senders that
  don't match any other rule in the record. An explicit "+all", or a bare
  "all" with no qualifier character (which defaults to +all per RFC 7208),
  tells receiving mail servers to accept mail from ANY sending host as
  authorized for the domain, defeating SPF's anti-spoofing purpose entirely.
  The safe values are "-all" (hard fail) or "~all" (soft fail).
remediation: |
  Use a restrictive qualifier on the "all" mechanism:

    resource "google_dns_record_set" "spf" {
      type    = "TXT"
      rrdatas = ["\"v=spf1 include:_spf.example.com -all\""]
    }
resources:
  google_dns_record_set:
    filter:
      path: type
      equals: TXT
    path: rrdatas
    none_match: "\\+all\\b|\\sall\\b"

suggested_policies.rationale: google_dns_managed_zone's 3 existing policies (HLD_GCP_027, HLD_GCP_132, HLD_GCP_271) cover DNSSEC and query logging only — none check for a CAA record. This is exactly the shape requires_companion was built for: an inbound google_dns_record_set referencing the zone via its `managed_zone` attribute (the same string-join pattern already used by aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration's `via: bucket` in encryption-at-rest.yaml), filtered by `where: type equals CAA`. No DSL extension needed. Scoped to non-private zones via `filter` since CAA is meaningless for internal-only zones that never get publicly-issued certs. Imported locally as HLD_GCP_470 and submitted upstream on branch feat/hld-gcp-470-caa-record-required (push succeeded to the JamesWoolfenden/holden fork; PR to PaloAltoNetworks/holden blocked by org SAML SSO from this session). Note: originally assigned HLD_GCP_468, renumbered to 470 for the same ID-collision reason as HLD_GCP_469 above. Confirmed limitation: requires_companion/via cannot resolve a companion's per-instance attribute when it is materialized through for_each + each.value (reproduces identically for a local, a variable, or a caller-supplied module argument) — a static/literal companion resource passes correctly. This module's own google_dns_managed_zone.main carries a holden:ignore:HLD_GCP_470 suppression citing this exact gap, since its google_dns_record_set.records is for_each-driven over var.records.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_470
name: Cloud DNS managed zones should have a CAA record restricting certificate issuance
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  A CAA (Certification Authority Authorization) record tells every
  CA/Browser-Forum-compliant certificate authority which CAs, if any, are
  allowed to issue certificates for the domain. Without one, any publicly
  trusted CA can issue a certificate for the zone's hostnames after passing
  domain validation alone, including a CA that is compromised or has a
  validation weakness. A CAA record is a cheap, standard control that
  narrows this to one or a small set of trusted issuers.
remediation: |
  Add a CAA record set restricting issuance to your chosen CA(s):

    resource "google_dns_record_set" "caa" {
      managed_zone = google_dns_managed_zone.main.name
      name         = google_dns_managed_zone.main.dns_name
      type         = "CAA"
      ttl          = 3600
      rrdatas      = ["0 issue \"letsencrypt.org\""]
    }
resources:
  google_dns_managed_zone:
    filter:
      path: visibility
      not_equals: private
    requires_companion:
      type: google_dns_record_set
      via: managed_zone
      where:
        path: type
        equals: CAA

suggested_suppressions.reason: google_dns_record_set.records (google_dns_record_set.records.tf) references this zone via managed_zone and, per the caller-supplied var.records in example/examplea/module.dns.tf, includes a CAA entry for holden-test.example.com. — but that record is materialized via for_each + each.value, so requires_companion's where: type equals CAA cannot resolve the per-instance each.value.type to a concrete value. Verified with an isolated static-resource fixture (no for_each) against the same policy YAML, which passed correctly, confirming this is a for_each/each.value resolution gap in the engine, not a real missing CAA record.
suggested_suppressions.suppression_comment: # holden:ignore:HLD_GCP_470: google_dns_record_set.records references this zone via managed_zone and includes a CAA entry (see example/examplea/module.dns.tf), but it's materialized via for_each + each.value which requires_companion's where clause can't resolve — confirmed for_each/each.value resolution gap, not a missing record
